form_analysis.feedback: Excellent aftercare form for general benign lesion removal covering various lesion types. Strong guidance on differentiation from malignant lesions and comprehensive healing protocols.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is for laser removal of various benign skin lesions: seborrheic keratoses, dermatosis papulosa nigra, syringomas, xanthelasma, etc. Each lesion type requires specific laser approach and aftercare.

instructions.general_directive: Follow lesion-specific guidance. Benign lesion removal is generally safe but requires proper diagnosis first.

sections.title: Lesion Types & Considerations
items: Dermatosis papulosa nigra: Small dark papules in darker skin.
Syringomas: Small flesh-colored bumps around eyes.
Xanthelasma: Yellow cholesterol deposits on eyelids.

sections.title: Pre-Removal Diagnosis Importance
sections.content: CRITICAL: Lesion must be properly diagnosed as benign before laser removal. If any doubt, biopsy first. Laser destroys tissue preventing later histology.

sections.title: Laser Selection by Lesion Type
items: Pigmented lesions: Q-switched laser for melanin.
Vascular lesions: Pulsed dye laser for blood vessels.
Raised lesions: CO₂ laser for ablation.
Combination lesions: May require multiple lasers.

sections.title: Healing Protocols Varied by Depth
items: Superficial lesions: 3-7 days healing, minimal care.
Deeper lesions: 7-14 days, more involved wound care.
Eyelid lesions (xanthelasma): Special care near eyes.
Facial lesions: More cosmetic concern, stricter scar prevention.

sections.title: Scar Management Principles
items: Massage after healing to prevent adhesions.
Consider early intervention for hypertrophic scarring.

sections.title: Recurrence Monitoring
sections.content: Some lesions may recur: 1) Xanthelasma may return if cholesterol high 2) Syringomas often recur 3) Seborrheic keratoses may develop new ones. Monitor for recurrence at 6-12 months.
